hyperedges.label: AST + Semantic Merge to Graph Pipeline

nodes.label: /graphify Skill (Kilo)
nodes.rationale: Turns any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into a persistent, queryable knowledge graph with an honest audit trail so cross-document connections surface without being asked about.

nodes.label: /graphify Skill (Droid)
nodes.rationale: Droid-host variant of the same pipeline; differs from the Kilo variant mainly in subagent dispatch conventions (Agent tool, subagent_type=general-purpose).

nodes.label: Step 0 - GitHub Repos and Multi-Path Merge
nodes.rationale: Only runs for URLs or several local subfolders; a plain local path skips it.

nodes.label: Step 1 - Ensure graphify Installed
nodes.rationale: Interpreter is resolved once (uv tool, then shebang, then python3) and written to .graphify_python so every later step uses the same environment across invocations.

nodes.label: Step 2 - Detect Files
nodes.rationale: The detect sidecar is written from Python rather than a shell redirect so the same block renders on PowerShell hosts without console-encoding drift (#2528).

nodes.label: Step 2.5 - Video and Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: Video/audio must become text before Step 3 so transcripts can be treated as doc files by semantic extraction.

nodes.label: Step 3 - Extract Entities and Relationships
nodes.rationale: Split into deterministic/free structural extraction and token-costing semantic extraction; the two run in parallel because they operate on different file types, saving 5-15s on large corpora.

nodes.label: Part A - AST Structural Extraction
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted structurally with no LLM and no API key at all, so a code-only corpus needs nothing beyond this pass.

nodes.label: Part B - Semantic Extraction (Parallel Subagents)
nodes.rationale: Subagents are mandatory because reading files one-by-one is 5-10x slower; a code-only corpus skips Part B entirely since AST already covers code.

nodes.label: No API Key Required Policy
nodes.rationale: graphify reads only GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY and never ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY; when no key is set the host agent itself is the LLM, so prompting for or blocking on a key is a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: Gemini Semantic Extraction Backend
nodes.rationale: Used instead of subagent dispatch when GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY is already set; default model gemini-3-flash-preview, overridable via GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL or --model.

nodes.label: Step B0 - Check Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Only document/paper/image go to semantic extraction because flattening every category makes subagents re-read every source file already covered by AST (#1392); the cached file is always rewritten or deleted so Part C never merges a stale .graphify_cached.json.

nodes.label: SPEC_PATH (extraction-spec.md prompt path)
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are attributed to the prompt that produced them, so a graphify upgrade that changes the prompt forces re-extraction instead of replaying stale entries (#1939).

nodes.label: references/extraction-spec.md
nodes.rationale: Loaded only when at least one chunk holds a doc, paper, or image; a pure-code corpus skips Part B and never reads it.

nodes.label: Step B1 - Split Into Chunks
nodes.rationale: Each image gets its own chunk because vision needs separate context; same-directory files are grouped so cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted.

nodes.label: Step B2 - Dispatch All Subagents in One Message
nodes.rationale: Multiple tool calls in the same response is the only way subagents run in parallel; sequential calls defeat the purpose. subagent_type must be general-purpose because Explore is read-only and silently drops chunk files.

nodes.label: CHUNK_PATH (absolute chunk output path)
nodes.rationale: Derived from cwd, not .graphify_root or the scan dir, because Part C globs graphify-out/ relative to cwd (#1392).

nodes.label: Step B3 - Collect, Cache, and Merge
nodes.rationale: Chunk file existence on disk is the success signal; a missing chunk means a read-only subagent and must warn rather than silently skip. Real token counts are read from the Agent result usage field because chunk JSON always carries placeholder zeros.

nodes.label: Part C - Merge AST + Semantic
nodes.rationale: AST nodes go first and semantic nodes are deduplicated by id, so structural truth wins over LLM inference on id collisions.

nodes.label: Step 4 - Build, Cluster, Analyze, Generate Outputs
nodes.rationale: root= mirrors the --update runbook so full builds and incremental updates never drift apart on re-extract (#1361).

nodes.label: Empty Graph Guard
nodes.rationale: Checked immediately after build and before any write so an empty extraction cannot clobber a good graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, or analysis sidecar (#1392).

nodes.label: Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json returns False and writes nothing when the new graph is smaller than the existing graph.json; report and sidecar are only written when the graph actually landed so they never describe a graph graph.json doesn't contain (#1392).

nodes.label: Step 4.5 - Graph Health Check
nodes.rationale: Read-only and never aborts, because the graph stays usable — but the integrity issue must be visible per the Honesty Rules. Surfaces the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches.

nodes.label: Step 5 - Label Communities
nodes.rationale: Re-exports so graph.json nodes carry the curated community_name (#2490); questions are regenerated because labels affect question phrasing.

nodes.label: Step 6 - Obsidian Vault (opt-in) + HTML
nodes.rationale: Obsidian is opt-in because it generates one file per node; HTML auto-aggregates to a community view above 5000 nodes.

nodes.label: Steps 6b-8 - Wiki, Neo4j, FalkorDB, SVG, GraphML, MCP
nodes.rationale: Flag-gated so a default run skips all of them; --wiki must run before Step 9 cleanup while .graphify_labels.json still exists.

nodes.label: Step 9 - Manifest, Cost Tracker, Cleanup, Report
nodes.rationale: Manifest keys are relativized to the scan root so the manifest is portable across clones/machines and a later --update matches cached files instead of missing every one (#1417).

nodes.label: Semantic Manifest Stamping Policy
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped, so a failed or omitted chunk stays unstamped and is re-queued rather than marked done and lost forever (#2015). Dispatched-but-unstamped files get their stale semantic_hash cleared (#1948), and scan_corpus uses the raw corpus so newly-excluded files are dropped rather than masquerading as deletions (#1908). Code is always stamped because AST is deterministic.

nodes.label: Fast Path - Existing Graph Query
nodes.rationale: If graphify-out/graph.json exists and the request is a natural-language question rather than an explicit rebuild, Steps 1-5 are skipped entirely — the graph is already built, so use it instead of re-detecting or asking the user to narrow.

nodes.label: /graphify query Flow
nodes.rationale: The question is expanded against the graph's own vocabulary before traversal so a wording mismatch does not collapse the answer to noise; answers use only graph output and quote source_location when citing a fact.

nodes.label: Interpreter Guard for Subcommands
nodes.rationale: Re-resolves the interpreter when .graphify_python is missing (e.g. the user deleted graphify-out/) so subcommands don't break; the shebang is character-validated before use and falls back to python3.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS when unsure), never skip the corpus warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion scores behind symbols, and never run HTML viz above 5000 nodes without warning.

nodes.label: Kilo-Specific Rules
nodes.rationale: Kilo uses the native Task tool with subagent_type=general for extraction fan-out, all launched in one response for parallelism; code edits during a session are followed by graphify update .

nodes.label: Honesty Rules (Droid)
nodes.rationale: Identical rule set to the Kilo variant: AMBIGUOUS over invention, mandatory corpus warning, visible token cost, raw cohesion numbers, and a 5000-node HTML viz warning.

nodes.label: graphify.build.build_from_json
nodes.rationale: directed=IS_DIRECTED selects a DiGraph preserving source→target when --directed is given, otherwise the default undirected Graph.

nodes.label: graphify.export.to_json
nodes.rationale: Returns False and writes nothing when the new graph would shrink an existing graph.json (#479).

nodes.label: graphify.cli._stamped_manifest_files
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the library extract path exactly so the skill runbook and the CLI stamp identically.

nodes.label: .graphify_python (interpreter sidecar)
nodes.rationale: Persisted across invocations so every subsequent bash block uses the same resolved interpreter instead of a bare python3.

nodes.label: .graphify_semantic.json
nodes.rationale: Written as an empty stub on a code-only corpus because Part C reads it unconditionally and would otherwise hit FileNotFoundError.

nodes.label: .graphify_labels.json
nodes.rationale: Consumed by the visualizer and the --wiki export, so wiki must run before Step 9 deletes the sidecars.

nodes.label: Guide-After-Pipeline Closing Protocol
nodes.rationale: Only God Nodes, Surprising Connections, and Suggested Questions are pasted, then the single most boundary-crossing question is offered — each answer ends with a follow-up so the session feels like navigation, not a one-shot report. The graph is the map; the agent is the guide.
